name: Titanium oxide, lambda phase
equilibrium_context: beta-Ti3O5 (semiconductor) and lambda-Ti3O5 (metallic); in the bulk a semiconductor-metal transition at about 460 K, in nanocrystals lambda is frozen in at room temperature
summary: The most extreme case of metastability in the register: bidirectionally photoswitchable at room temperature, both phases stable essentially indefinitely. The mechanism is uncontroversially NOT purely electronic - precisely the counterpart to VO2.

driven_states.emergent_property: A single laser pulse switches beta to lambda (semiconductor to metal) and back, at room temperature, bidirectionally and repeatably. Both phases are persistent. First photorewritable metal oxide state at room temperature.
driven_states.quenchable_by: second laser pulse of a different wavelength
driven_states.source: Ohkoshi et al., Nature Chemistry 2, 539 (2010), doi:10.1038/nchem.670
further_sources: Mariette et al., Nat. Commun. 12 (2021), doi:10.1038/s41467-021-21316-y (strain wave pathway, time-resolved X-ray powder diffraction)
Commun. Mater. (2025), doi:10.1038/s43246-025-00896-y (anisotropic phase separation, fluence thresholds)
driven_states.caveat: To be honest: the case is largely thermally or strain-driven, not electronic. The 2025 work shows that after 100 ps the transformation is carried by heat diffusion, with crystallite-size-dependent time constants of 40 to 180 ns. The value lies not in the mechanism but in the robust bistability: here metastability is uncontroversial. Damage threshold about 80 mJ/cm^2.

sources: Ohkoshi et al., Nature Chemistry 2, 539 (2010), doi:10.1038/nchem.670

gaps: The lifetime is given as a lower bound; it is limited by thermal activation over a real energy barrier, and has not been measured.
